Yes, in this snapshot `Path` exposes `move_into`, and it was added in Python 3.14.

The pathlib documentation describes `Path.move_into(target_dir)`. It moves a file or directory tree into an existing directory and returns a new `Path` pointing to the moved path. It carries the note `.. versionadded:: 3.14`.

Source: `library/pathlib.rst`
